plan: Candidate004 collapses the whole RMSNorm into a single custom torch.autograd.Function so the native autograd branch for rstd is no longer retained, which was the remaining dispatch cost in candidate003. All native BF16 arithmetic, ordering, and reductions are preserved exactly; tolerances are unchanged. FORWARD (inside the Function, no tracked native graph): x_c=x.contiguous(); v=x_c.pow(2).mean(-1,keepdim=True); v.add_(1.0013580322265625e-05) in-place (BF16 eps literal = BF16(1e-5)); r=rsqrt(v) — all BF16, identical to native. Then the candidate003 cached-compiled forward affine kernel writes native-BF16 t=bf16(x*r) and y=bf16(t*w); save x_c, r, weight_c, t. BACKWARD uses the independently probed exact BF16 analytic sequence (verified exact dx/dw at x-scales 0/.01/1/10). Pass1 Triton elementwise kernel: gw=BF16(g*w); dr_terms=BF16(gw*x) (using the rounded gw); dw_terms=BF16(g*t); it writes gw and the two term buffers as BF16. Native Torch then does the UNCHANGED reductions dr=dr_terms.sum_to_size(r.shape) and dw=dw_terms.sum_to_size(weight.shape) — no reduction fused or reordered. Pass2 Triton pointwise kernel computes dx with an explicit .to(bfloat16).to(float32) barrier after EACH native stage, in native order: cube=BF16((r*r)*r) (one rounding, matching r.pow(3) which multiplies in float32 then rounds once); scale=BF16(-0.5*cube); dv=BF16(dr*scale); dsq=BF16(dv/512); two_x=BF16(2*x); extra=BF16(dsq*two_x); direct=BF16(gw*r); dx=BF16(direct+extra). No rsqrt approximation is introduced because the saved native r is reused. Backward returns (dx, dw). Only tensors required for autograd are saved; nothing persistent (inputs/outputs/grads/RNG/results) is cached. LAUNCH: three separate process-local code-only runner dicts (_FWD_RUNNERS, _BWD1_RUNNERS, _BWD2_RUNNERS) keyed by (x.device.index, numel, hidden); the first call for a key performs a real JIT launch (producing real output) then stores compiled[(grid0,1,1)]; later calls invoke the cached closure on fresh actual tensor args with dynamic scalar numel/N and NO constexpr BLOCK. This caches compiled launch closures only, never results; every call executes; the installed closure re-reads the current CUDA stream so no stale stream/pointer is captured. The vendor-unsupported enable_fp_fusion keyword is omitted entirely; the per-stage BF16 barriers independently prevent any undesired fused multiply-add from changing rounding. Guards accept only nonempty BF16 CUDA tensors with hidden=512, 1D weight=512, x and weight on the same CUDA device, and eps exactly 1e-5, else NotImplementedError for native fallback. Input may be 3D/strided: .contiguous() is differentiable, dx is returned in the input shape and dw in weight shape. No files/env/network/benchmark-mode/source mutation. This is portable pointwise fusion with no NVIDIA-specific mechanism. No speed claim is made — warmup(20) vs formal timed steps and the full FP32-gradient-accumulation/master-weight/BF16-param 3-step comparator must be measured by the independent verifier.
risks: The analytic backward assumes native r.pow(3) rounds once (float32 r*r*r then a single BF16 cast). If the vendor Torch/compiler evaluates pow(3) with a different internal product order or intermediate rounding, cube and hence dx could differ; this is the single most likely rejection cause and is mirrored faithfully in pass2 but not independently guaranteed on BI-V150.

dx now comes entirely from a hand-written analytic formula rather than Torch autograd of the native branch; any stage whose BF16 rounding order differs from native (e.g. -0.5*cube vs cube*-0.5, dv/512 vs mean-grad path) would break exactness even though the probe matched at four scales.

Caching relies on the vendor CompiledKernel contract (kernel[grid](...) returns a CompiledKernel; compiled[(grid0,1,1)] yields a stream-reading launch closure) and the exact positional arity (fwd 7, bwd1 7, bwd2 5 tensor/scalar args before constexpr); a toolchain change to this API would break the steady-state path.
Runner dict population is not lock-guarded; concurrent first-touch per key may JIT-compile more than once (idempotent, data/stream-independent), an untested concurrency path.
Three full-size intermediate buffers in pass1 (gw, dr_terms, dw_terms) plus dx increase memory traffic; the launch reduction may still not beat native on the small [256,512] workload.
No speed improvement is claimed; exactness (standalone CPU gates and the 3-step FP32-master/BF16-param training comparator) governs promotion and may still reject this candidate.
